# Visium HD Data Analysis Workflow - 16um Binned

This is a comprehensive workflow for analyzing Visium HD spatial transcriptomics data at **16um bin resolution**. The workflow includes data loading, quality control, normalization, clustering, and spatial analysis.

## 1. Data Loading and Initial Setup

### 1.1 Configure Analysis Parameters

```{r parameters}
# =============================================================================
# ANALYSIS PARAMETERS - MODIFY THESE FOR YOUR DATASET
# =============================================================================

# Sample information
sample.names <- c("SHNA03_D3-7um_0_v1","SHNA03_D4-7um_0_v1","SHNA03_I2-7um_0_v1","SHNA03_I3-7um_0_v1")  # Update with your sample names
# Space Ranger output root, one folder per sample.
data.dir <- Sys.getenv("CHERRYPIC_RAWDATA", "rawdata")
bin.size <- c(16)  # Bin size for analysis - 16um bins

# Image names for each sample (if multiple images per sample)
image.names <- list(
  "SHNA03_D3-7um_0_v1"= c("Duodenum-3"),  # Update with your image names
  "SHNA03_D4-7um_0_v1"= c("Duodenum-4"),
  "SHNA03_I2-7um_0_v1"= c("Ileum-2"),
  "SHNA03_I3-7um_0_v1"= c("Ileum-3")
)

# QC thresholds - adjusted for 16um bins (larger bins = higher counts expected)
min.counts <- 50      # Minimum UMI counts per spot (higher for 16um vs 8um)
max.mt.percent <- 20  # Maximum mitochondrial gene percentage

# Clustering parameters
sketch.ncells <- 5000  # Number of cells for sketching
cluster.resolutions <- c(0.2, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4)  # Clustering resolutions to test

# Spatial analysis parameters
banksy.lambda <- c(0.2, 0.8)  # BANKSY lambda values
banksy.k <- c(15, 20)          # BANKSY k-neighbors
```

### 1.2 Load Visium HD Data

```{r load_data}
# Minimal function to load Visium HD data (with image)
load_visium_hd_data <- function(sample.name, data.dir, bin.size) {
  # Construct the path to the spatial directory for the given bin size
  spatial.dir <- file.path(data.dir, sample.name)
  if (!dir.exists(spatial.dir)) {
    warning("Spatial directory not found: ", spatial.dir)
    return(NULL)
  }
  # Load the data and image
  object <- Load10X_Spatial(data.dir = spatial.dir, bin.size = bin.size, slice = image.names[[sample.name]])
  cat("Loaded sample:", sample.name, "with", ncol(object), "spots\n")
  return(object)
}

# Load all samples
object.list <- lapply(sample.names, function(sample.name) {
  load_visium_hd_data(sample.name, data.dir, bin.size[1])
})
names(object.list) <- sample.names
object.list <- object.list[!sapply(object.list, is.null)]
cat("Successfully loaded", length(object.list), "samples\n")
```

### 1.3 Split Multi-Image Samples (if applicable)

```{r split_samples}
# Function to split samples with multiple images
split_multi_image_samples <- function(object.list, image.names) {
  split.object.list <- list()
  
  for (sample.name in names(object.list)) {
    obj <- object.list[[sample.name]]
    images <- image.names[[sample.name]]
    
    if (length(images) > 1) {
      # If CSV files exist for image splitting
      csv.dir <- file.path(dirname(obj@images[[1]]@image), "cloupe_csvs")
      
      if (dir.exists(csv.dir)) {
        csv.files <- list.files(csv.dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
        
        for (i in seq_along(images)) {
          image.name <- images[i]
          csv.file <- csv.files[grep(image.name, csv.files)][1]
          
          if (!is.na(csv.file) && file.exists(csv.file)) {
            cells.to.keep <- read.csv(csv.file)$Barcode
            sub.obj <- subset(obj, cells = cells.to.keep)
            sub.obj$orig.ident <- image.name
            sub.obj$sample <- sample.name
            
            split.object.list[[paste(sample.name, image.name, sep = "_")]] <- sub.obj
          }
        }
      } else {
        # If no CSV files, keep the whole sample
        obj$orig.ident <- sample.name
        obj$sample <- sample.name
        split.object.list[[sample.name]] <- obj
      }
    } else {
      # Single image sample
      obj$orig.ident <- images[1]
      obj$sample <- sample.name
      split.object.list[[sample.name]] <- obj
    }
  }
  
  return(split.object.list)
}

# Split samples if needed
split.object.list <- split_multi_image_samples(object.list, image.names)
cat("After splitting:", length(split.object.list), "objects\n")
```

## 2. Quality Control Analysis

### 2.1 Calculate QC Metrics

```{r qc_metrics}
# Calculate mitochondrial gene percentage
split.object.list <- lapply(split.object.list, function(obj) {
  obj <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, pattern = "^mt-|^MT-", col.name = "percent.mt")
  return(obj)
})

# Get assay name dynamically (should be Spatial.016um for 16um bins)
assay.name <- names(split.object.list[[1]]@assays)[1]
count.col <- paste0("nCount_", assay.name)
feature.col <- paste0("nFeature_", assay.name)

cat("Using assay:", assay.name, "\n")
cat("Count column:", count.col, "\n")
cat("Feature column:", feature.col, "\n")
```

### 2.3 Apply QC Filters

```{r qc_filter}
# Apply QC filters - dynamically handle column name
filtered.object.list <- lapply(split.object.list, function(obj) {
  cat("Before filtering:", ncol(obj), "spots\n")
  
  # Get the count column dynamically
  count.col.local <- grep('^nCount_Spatial', colnames(obj@meta.data), value = TRUE)[1]
  if (is.na(count.col.local)) stop('No nCount_Spatial column found in metadata!')
  
  cat("Using count column:", count.col.local, "\n")
  
  # Filter based on metadata
  cells.keep <- obj@meta.data[[count.col.local]] >= min.counts
  obj <- obj[, cells.keep]
  
  cat("After filtering:", ncol(obj), "spots\n")
  return(obj)
})

# Summary of filtering
cat("\nFiltering Summary:\n")
for (obj.name in names(filtered.object.list)) {
  original <- ncol(split.object.list[[obj.name]])
  filtered <- ncol(filtered.object.list[[obj.name]])
  cat(obj.name, ":", original, "->", filtered, 
      "(", round(100 * filtered/original, 1), "%)\n")
}
```

## 3. Data Integration and Normalization

### 3.1 Normalize and Merge Data

```{r normalize_merge}
# Normalize each sample individually
normalized.object.list <- lapply(filtered.object.list, function(obj) {
  obj <- NormalizeData(obj, assay = assay.name)
  return(obj)
})

# Merge all samples
if (length(normalized.object.list) > 1) {
  merged.object <- merge(normalized.object.list[[1]], 
                        normalized.object.list[2:length(normalized.object.list)])
} else {
  merged.object <- normalized.object.list[[1]]
}

cat("Merged object dimensions:", dim(merged.object), "\n")
```

### 3.2 Sketching for Large Datasets

```{r sketching}
# Set default assay
DefaultAssay(merged.object) <- assay.name

# Find variable features
merged.object <- FindVariableFeatures(merged.object)
merged.object <- ScaleData(merged.object)

# Create sketch for large datasets
merged.object <- SketchData(
  object = merged.object,
  ncells = 5000L,
  method = "Uniform",
  sketched.assay = "sketch"
)

cat("Sketched", sketch.ncells, "cells for downstream analysis\n")
```

## 4. Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering

### 4.1 PCA and Clustering on Sketched Data

```{r clustering}
# Switch to sketched assay
DefaultAssay(merged.object) <- "sketch"

# Perform clustering workflow on sketched data
merged.object <- FindVariableFeatures(merged.object)
merged.object <- ScaleData(merged.object)
merged.object <- RunPCA(merged.object, assay = "sketch", reduction.name = "pca.sketch")
merged.object <- FindNeighbors(merged.object, assay = "sketch", 
                              reduction = "pca.sketch", dims = 1:50)
merged.object <- FindClusters(merged.object, resolution = cluster.resolutions)
merged.object <- RunUMAP(merged.object, reduction = "pca.sketch", 
                        reduction.name = "umap.sketch", return.model = TRUE, dims = 1:50)
```

### 4.2 Project Results to Full Dataset

```{r projection}
# Project clustering results to full dataset
merged.object <- ProjectData(
  object = merged.object,
  assay = assay.name,
  full.reduction = "full.pca.sketch",
  sketched.assay = "sketch",
  sketched.reduction = "pca.sketch",
  umap.model = "umap.sketch",
  dims = 1:50,
  refdata = setNames(
    lapply(cluster.resolutions, function(res) paste0("sketch_snn_res.", res)),
    paste0("sketch_snn_res.", cluster.resolutions)
  )
)

# Save intermediate results
saveRDS(merged.object, file = "output_16um/RDS-files/merged_object_clustered_16um.RDS")
cat("Saved clustered object\n")
```

## 5. Cluster Visualization and Analysis

### 5.1 UMAP Visualization

```{r umap_viz, fig.width=16, fig.height=12}
# =============================================================================
# UMAP PLOTS - SKETCHED DATA ONLY (4 plots per page)
# =============================================================================

DefaultAssay(merged.object) <- "sketch"

# Create UMAP plots for all resolutions
cat("Generating UMAP plots for", length(cluster.resolutions), "resolutions...\n")


# --- Save UMAP plots as annotated ggplot2 objects for easier editing ---
umap_annotated_list <- list()
for (i in seq_along(cluster.resolutions)) {
  res <- cluster.resolutions[i]
  colname <- paste0("sketch_snn_res.", res)
  if (colname %in% colnames(merged.object@meta.data)) {
    Idents(merged.object) <- colname
    p <- DimPlot(
      merged.object,
      reduction = "umap.sketch",
      group.by = colname,
      label = TRUE,
      repel = TRUE,
      pt.size = 1.5,
      cols = custom_colors,
      raster = FALSE
    ) +
      ggtitle(paste("UMAP (sketch) - Resolution", res)) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 18)
    umap_annotated_list[[paste0("res_", res)]] <- p
    # Save each plot as an RDS file for later editing
    saveRDS(p, file = paste0("output_16um/plots/umap_sketch_annotated_res_", res, ".rds"))
  }
}

# Optionally, save all plots in a single RDS list for batch editing
saveRDS(umap_annotated_list, file = "output_16um/plots/umap_sketch_annotated_all_res.rds")

# Also save as PDF for quick viewing (4 per page)
pdf("output_16um/plots/umap_multiple_resolutions.pdf", height = 12, width = 16)
n_plots <- length(umap_annotated_list)
n_pages <- ceiling(n_plots / 4)
umap.plots <- unname(umap_annotated_list)
for (page in 1:n_pages) {
  start_idx <- (page - 1) * 4 + 1
  end_idx <- min(page * 4, n_plots)
  plots_this_page <- umap.plots[start_idx:end_idx]
  while (length(plots_this_page) < 4) {
    plots_this_page[[length(plots_this_page) + 1]] <- ggplot() + theme_void()
  }
  print(wrap_plots(plots_this_page, ncol = 2, nrow = 2))
}
dev.off()

cat("UMAP annotated plots (sketched data) saved as .rds and PDF in output_16um/plots/\n")
cat("Total pages:", n_pages, "\n")
```

### 5.2 Clustree Analysis - Resolution Selection

```{r clustree_analysis, fig.width=14, fig.height=12}
# =============================================================================
# CLUSTREE ANALYSIS - VISUALIZE CLUSTER STABILITY ACROSS RESOLUTIONS
# =============================================================================

library(clustree)

cat("Generating clustree analysis for resolution selection...\n")

# Check available clustering columns
cluster_cols <- grep("sketch_snn_res", colnames(merged.object@meta.data), value = TRUE)
cat("Available clustering columns:", paste(cluster_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# IMPORTANT: Remove the .score columns that interfere with clustree parsing
# Keep only the actual cluster assignment columns (not the .score columns)
cluster_cols_clean <- cluster_cols[!grepl("\\.score$", cluster_cols)]
cat("Clustering columns for clustree:", paste(cluster_cols_clean, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Create a subset of metadata with only the required columns for clustree
metadata_for_clustree <- merged.object@meta.data[, cluster_cols_clean, drop = FALSE]

# Clustree plot showing cluster relationships across resolutions
pdf("output_16um/plots/clustree_resolution_analysis.pdf", height = 14, width = 12)

# Basic clustree plot
p_clustree <- clustree(metadata_for_clustree, prefix = "sketch_snn_res.") +
  ggtitle("Clustree: Cluster Stability Across Resolutions (16um)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
print(p_clustree)

# Clustree with SC3 stability metric
p_clustree_stability <- clustree(metadata_for_clustree, prefix = "sketch_snn_res.", 
                                  node_colour = "sc3_stability") +
  ggtitle("Clustree: Colored by SC3 Stability (16um)") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma")
print(p_clustree_stability)

dev.off()

# Also save as PNG for easier viewing
png("output_16um/plots/clustree_resolution_analysis.png", height = 1200, width = 1000, res = 100)
print(p_clustree)
dev.off()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLUSTER COUNT SUMMARY
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n--- Cluster Count Summary by Resolution ---\n")
cluster_summary <- data.frame(
  Resolution = cluster.resolutions,
  NumClusters = sapply(cluster.resolutions, function(res) {
    col_name <- paste0("sketch_snn_res.", res)
    if (col_name %in% colnames(merged.object@meta.data)) {
      length(unique(merged.object@meta.data[[col_name]]))
    } else {
      NA
    }
  })
)
print(cluster_summary)

# Save summary
write.csv(cluster_summary, "output_16um/tables/cluster_count_by_resolution.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nClustree analysis complete!\n")
cat("Review the clustree plots to identify the optimal resolution.\n")
cat("Look for: stable branches (less mixing between resolutions)\n")
```

```{r spatial_viz, fig.width=20, fig.height=16}
for (res in cluster.resolutions) {

      height = 12, width = 20)
  
  p <- SpatialDimPlot(merged.object, 
                     group.by = paste0("sketch_snn_res.", res),
                     label = TRUE, repel = TRUE, label.size = 4,
                     pt.size.factor = 1.5, cols = custom_colors) +
    ggtitle(paste("Spatial Clusters 16um - Resolution", res)) +
    theme(legend.position = "right")
  print(p)
  
  dev.off()
}
cat("Spatial cluster plots completed for all resolutions!\n")

# =============================================================================
# INDIVIDUAL CLUSTER HIGHLIGHTING
# =============================================================================

# Get the image names from the merged object
available.images <- Images(merged.object)
cat("Available images in merged object:", paste(available.images, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 1: Combined plots (all samples together) for each cluster
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n--- Generating COMBINED individual cluster plots (all samples) ---\n")

for (res in cluster.resolutions) {
  cat("Generating combined cluster plots for resolution", res, "\n")
  
  Idents(merged.object) <- paste0("sketch_snn_res.", res)
  clusters.to.plot <- sort(unique(as.character(Idents(merged.object))))
  
  # Create PDF for combined view (all samples)
  pdf(paste0("output_16um/plots/individual_clusters_combined_res_", res, ".pdf"), 
      height = 10, width = 14)
  
  for (cluster in clusters.to.plot) {
    # Get cells in this cluster using CellsByIdentities (returns proper format)
    cells <- CellsByIdentities(merged.object, idents = cluster)
    
    # Get the custom color for this cluster
    cluster_color <- ifelse(as.character(cluster) %in% names(custom_colors), 
                           custom_colors[as.character(cluster)], 
                           "red")
    
    p <- SpatialDimPlot(merged.object,
                       cells.highlight = cells,
                       cols.highlight = c(cluster_color, "grey90"),
                       pt.size.factor = 1.5) +
      theme(legend.position = "none") +
      ggtitle(paste("All Samples - Cluster", cluster, "- Resolution", res, "(16um)"))
    print(p)
  }
  dev.off()
}
cat("Combined cluster plots completed!\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 2: Separate plots for each sample/image
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n--- Generating SEPARATE individual cluster plots (per sample) ---\n")

for (res in cluster.resolutions) {
  cat("Generating per-sample cluster plots for resolution", res, "\n")
  
  Idents(merged.object) <- paste0("sketch_snn_res.", res)
  clusters.to.plot <- sort(unique(as.character(Idents(merged.object))))
  
  # Loop through each image (which corresponds to each sample)
  for (img.name in available.images) {
    cat("  Processing image:", img.name, "\n")
    
    # Create PDF for this image and resolution
    pdf(paste0("output_16um/plots/individual_clusters_res_", res, "_", 
               gsub("[^[:alnum:]]", "_", img.name), ".pdf"), 
        height = 8, width = 12)
    
    for (cluster in clusters.to.plot) {
      # Get cells in this cluster
      cells <- CellsByIdentities(merged.object, idents = cluster)
      
      # Get the custom color for this cluster (consistent across samples)
      cluster_color <- ifelse(as.character(cluster) %in% names(custom_colors), 
                             custom_colors[as.character(cluster)], 
                             "red")
      
      p <- SpatialDimPlot(merged.object,
                         images = img.name,
                         cells.highlight = cells,
                         cols.highlight = c(cluster_color, "grey90"),
                         pt.size.factor = 1.5) +
        theme(legend.position = "none",
              plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = -10)) +
        ggtitle(paste(img.name, "- Cluster", cluster, "- Resolution", res, "(16um)"))
      print(p)
    }
    dev.off()
  }
}
```

## 7. Spatial Analysis with BANKSY

### 7.1 BANKSY Setup and Analysis

```{r banksy_setup}
# Load BANKSY libraries
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Banksy)
  library(SeuratWrappers)
})

# Prepare data for BANKSY
merged.object <- NormalizeData(merged.object, assay = assay.name)
merged.object <- FindVariableFeatures(merged.object, nfeatures = 5000)

# Get consensus variable features across samples if multiple samples
if (length(unique(merged.object$orig.ident)) > 1) {
  # This would need custom implementation based on your specific needs
  # For now, use standard variable features
  consensus.var.feats <- VariableFeatures(merged.object)
} else {
  consensus.var.feats <- VariableFeatures(merged.object)
}

VariableFeatures(merged.object) <- consensus.var.feats
```

### 7.2 Prepare Spatial Coordinates

```{r banksy_coords}
# Extract spatial coordinates
locs.df.list <- lapply(unique(merged.object$orig.ident), function(sample_name) {
  # Get the image name for this sample
  available_images <- names(merged.object@images)
  image_name <- available_images[grepl(sample_name, available_images)][1]
  
  if (!is.na(image_name)) {
    loc.df <- GetTissueCoordinates(merged.object, image = image_name)
    return(loc.df)
  } else {
    # Fallback: use first available image
    loc.df <- GetTissueCoordinates(merged.object, image = available_images[1])
    return(loc.df)
  }
})

names(locs.df.list) <- unique(merged.object$orig.ident)
locs.df <- bind_rows(locs.df.list, .id = "orig.ident")
colnames(locs.df) <- c("orig.ident", "dimx", "dimy", "cell")

# Add coordinates to metadata
merged.object <- AddMetaData(merged.object, metadata = locs.df)
```

### 7.3 Run BANKSY Analysis

```{r banksy_analysis}
# Run BANKSY for different lambda values
for (lambda.val in banksy.lambda) {
  for (k.val in banksy.k) {
    cat("Running BANKSY with lambda =", lambda.val, "and k =", k.val, "\n")
    
    assay.banksy.name <- paste0("BANKSY_l", lambda.val, "_k", k.val)
    
    try({
      merged.object <- RunBanksy(merged.object,
        lambda = lambda.val,
        assay_name = assay.banksy.name,
        group = "orig.ident",
        verbose = FALSE,
        dimx = "dimx",
        dimy = "dimy",
        split.scale = TRUE,
        assay = assay.name,
        slot = "data",
        features = "variable",
        k_geom = k.val
      )
      
      # Run clustering on BANKSY features
      DefaultAssay(merged.object) <- assay.banksy.name
      merged.object <- RunPCA(merged.object, assay = assay.banksy.name, 
                             reduction.name = paste0("pca.banksy_l", lambda.val, "_k", k.val),
                             features = rownames(merged.object), npcs = 30)
      merged.object <- FindNeighbors(merged.object, 
                                   reduction = paste0("pca.banksy_l", lambda.val, "_k", k.val),
                                   dims = 1:30)
      merged.object <- FindClusters(merged.object, 
                                  cluster.name = paste0("banksy_l", lambda.val, "_k", k.val, "_res.", cluster.resolutions),
                                  resolution = cluster.resolutions)
      
      cat("BANKSY analysis completed for lambda =", lambda.val, "k =", k.val, "\n")
    })
  }
}

gc()  # Garbage collection
```

## 8. Final Analysis and Export

### 8.1 Cluster Composition Analysis

```{r composition_analysis, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# Analyze cluster composition across samples for ALL resolutions

# Loop through all resolutions and generate composition plots
for (res in cluster.resolutions) {
  cat("\nGenerating composition plots for resolution", res, "\n")
  
  cluster.col <- paste0("sketch_snn_res.", res)
  
  # Check if this clustering exists
  if (!cluster.col %in% colnames(merged.object@meta.data)) {
    cat("Warning: Column", cluster.col, "not found. Skipping...\n")
    next
  }
  
  # Composition: Clusters per Sample
  composition.df <- merged.object@meta.data %>%
    select(orig.ident, all_of(cluster.col)) %>%
    group_by(orig.ident, !!sym(cluster.col)) %>%
    summarise(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(orig.ident) %>%
    mutate(percentage = counts / sum(counts) * 100)
  
  # Composition bar plot - Clusters per Sample
  p1 <- ggplot(composition.df, aes(x = orig.ident, y = percentage, 
                                  fill = !!sym(cluster.col))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    labs(title = paste("Cluster Composition 16um - Resolution", res),
         x = "Sample", y = "Percentage", fill = "Cluster")
  
  print(p1)
  
  # Composition: Samples per Cluster (flipped view)
  composition.df2 <- merged.object@meta.data %>%
    select(orig.ident, all_of(cluster.col)) %>%
    group_by(!!sym(cluster.col), orig.ident) %>%
    summarise(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(!!sym(cluster.col)) %>%
    mutate(percentage = counts / sum(counts) * 100)
  
  p2 <- ggplot(composition.df2, aes(x = !!sym(cluster.col), y = percentage, 
                                   fill = orig.ident)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    labs(title = paste("Sample Composition 16um - Resolution", res),
         x = "Cluster", y = "Percentage", fill = "Sample")
  
  print(p2)
  
  # Save plots for this resolution
  pdf(paste0("output_16um/plots/cluster_composition_res_", res, ".pdf"), width = 14, height = 8)
  print(p1)
  print(p2)
  dev.off()
  
  # Save composition data for this resolution
  write.csv(composition.df, 
            paste0("output_16um/tables/cluster_composition_by_sample_res_", res, ".csv"), 
            row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(composition.df2, 
            paste0("output_16um/tables/sample_composition_by_cluster_res_", res, ".csv"), 
            row.names = FALSE)
}

cat("\nCluster composition analysis completed for all resolutions!\n")
```

### 8.2 Add Cluster Annotations (Resolution 2)

```{r cluster_annotations, fig.width=20, fig.height=16, fig.show='hide'}
# =============================================================================
# ADD CLUSTER ANNOTATIONS FROM CSV FILE
# =============================================================================

# Load cluster annotations for resolution 2
# CSV columns: Cluster, Annotation, Spatial.region.annotation, Region.Annotation,
#              Compartment, Color, Granular.annotation, Granular.color
annotation.file <- "16um-binned-updated-annotations(res2).csv"

if (file.exists(annotation.file)) {
  cat("Loading cluster annotations from:", annotation.file, "\n")

  annotations <- read.csv(annotation.file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # Display summary
  cat("\nCluster Annotations Summary:\n")
  print(annotations[, c("Cluster", "Annotation", "Spatial.region.annotation",
                         "Region.Annotation", "Compartment", "Color")])

  # Remove rows with NA/empty Cluster
  annotations <- annotations[!is.na(annotations$Cluster) & annotations$Cluster != "", ]

  # Helper: replace NA/empty/"NA" with a fill value
  fill_na <- function(x, fill = "Unknown") {
    x[is.na(x) | x == "" | x == "NA"] <- fill
    x
  }

  annotations$Annotation                <- fill_na(annotations$Annotation)
  annotations$Spatial.region.annotation <- fill_na(annotations$Spatial.region.annotation)
  annotations$Region.Annotation         <- fill_na(annotations$Region.Annotation)
  annotations$Compartment               <- fill_na(annotations$Compartment)
  annotations$Granular.annotation       <- fill_na(annotations$Granular.annotation)

  # Create cluster-to-value mappings
  cid <- as.character(annotations$Cluster)

  cluster.to.annotation  <- setNames(annotations$Annotation,                cid)
  cluster.to.region      <- setNames(annotations$Spatial.region.annotation, cid)
  cluster.to.location    <- setNames(annotations$Region.Annotation,         cid)
  cluster.to.compartment <- setNames(annotations$Compartment,               cid)
  cluster.to.granular    <- setNames(annotations$Granular.annotation,       cid)

  # Map to all cells using resolution 2 clusters
  cell.clusters <- as.character(merged.object$sketch_snn_res.2)

  cluster_annotation_vec     <- fill_na(cluster.to.annotation[cell.clusters])
  region_annotation_vec      <- fill_na(cluster.to.region[cell.clusters])
  location_annotation_vec    <- fill_na(cluster.to.location[cell.clusters])
  compartment_annotation_vec <- fill_na(cluster.to.compartment[cell.clusters])
  granular_annotation_vec    <- fill_na(cluster.to.granular[cell.clusters])

  # Add all annotations to metadata
  merged.object <- AddMetaData(merged.object, metadata = data.frame(
    cluster_annotation     = cluster_annotation_vec,
    region_annotation      = region_annotation_vec,
    location_annotation    = location_annotation_vec,
    compartment_annotation = compartment_annotation_vec,
    granular_annotation    = granular_annotation_vec,
    row.names = colnames(merged.object)
  ))

  cat("\nAnnotations added to metadata:\n")
  cat("- cluster_annotation (broad)\n- region_annotation\n- location_annotation\n")
  cat("- compartment_annotation\n- granular_annotation\n")

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # BUILD COLOR PALETTES FROM CSV HEX CODES
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # Helper: build named color vector (annotation name → hex), deduplicating by name
  make_color_map <- function(ann_names, colors, fallback = custom_colors) {
    valid <- !is.na(colors) & colors != "" & colors != "NA"
    cmap  <- setNames(colors[valid], ann_names[valid])
    cmap  <- cmap[!duplicated(names(cmap))]
    # Fill any annotation not covered by the CSV Color column
    missing <- setdiff(unique(ann_names), names(cmap))
    if (length(missing) > 0) {
      extra <- fallback[which(!fallback %in% cmap)][seq_along(missing)]
      cmap  <- c(cmap, setNames(extra, missing))
    }
    cmap
  }

  # Broad cluster annotation colors (from Color column)
  annotation_colors   <- make_color_map(annotations$Annotation, annotations$Color)

  # Granular annotation colors (from Granular.color column)
  granular_colors     <- make_color_map(annotations$Granular.annotation, annotations$Granular.color)

  # Spatial region colors (reuse Color column, keyed by region name)
  region_colors       <- make_color_map(annotations$Spatial.region.annotation, annotations$Color)

  # Location (proximal/distal/both) - fixed palette
  unique_locations    <- unique(location_annotation_vec)
  location_colors     <- setNames(
    c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8", "#4DAF4A", "#984EA3", "#FF7F00")[seq_along(unique_locations)],
    unique_locations
  )

  # Compartment colors - fixed palette
  unique_compartments <- unique(compartment_annotation_vec)
  compartment_colors  <- setNames(
    c("#1B9E77", "#D95F02", "#7570B3", "#E7298A", "#66A61E")[seq_along(unique_compartments)],
    unique_compartments
  )

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # VISUALIZATION: UMAP with Annotations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  p_umap_annot <- DimPlot(merged.object,
                          reduction = "full.umap.sketch",
                          group.by = "cluster_annotation",
                          label = TRUE, label.size = 3, repel = TRUE,
                          raster = FALSE, pt.size = 1.5,
                          cols = annotation_colors) +
    ggtitle("UMAP - Broad Cluster Annotations (16um, res=2)") +
    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

  p_umap_gran <- DimPlot(merged.object,
                         reduction = "full.umap.sketch",
                         group.by = "granular_annotation",
                         label = TRUE, label.size = 3, repel = TRUE,
                         raster = FALSE, pt.size = 1.5,
                         cols = granular_colors) +
    ggtitle("UMAP - Granular Annotations (16um, res=2)") +
    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

  p_umap_region <- DimPlot(merged.object,
                           reduction = "full.umap.sketch",
                           group.by = "region_annotation",
                           label = TRUE, label.size = 4,
                           raster = FALSE, pt.size = 1.5,
                           cols = region_colors) +
    ggtitle("UMAP - Region Annotations (16um)")

  p_umap_compartment <- DimPlot(merged.object,
                                reduction = "full.umap.sketch",
                                group.by = "compartment_annotation",
                                label = TRUE, label.size = 4,
                                raster = FALSE, pt.size = 1.5,
                                cols = compartment_colors) +
    ggtitle("UMAP - Compartment Annotations (16um)")

  ggsave("output_16um/plots/umap_annotations_res2_cluster.pdf",     plot = p_umap_annot,       height = 12, width = 16)
  ggsave("output_16um/plots/umap_annotations_res2_granular.pdf",    plot = p_umap_gran,        height = 12, width = 16)
  ggsave("output_16um/plots/umap_annotations_res2_region.pdf",      plot = p_umap_region,      height = 12, width = 16)
  ggsave("output_16um/plots/umap_annotations_res2_compartment.pdf", plot = p_umap_compartment, height = 12, width = 16)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # VISUALIZATION: Spatial plots with Annotations (per-image, using ggsave)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  available.images <- Images(merged.object)

  spatial_annot_list <- list(
    list(group = "cluster_annotation",     cols = annotation_colors,   title = "Cluster_Annotations"),
    list(group = "granular_annotation",    cols = granular_colors,     title = "Granular_Annotations"),
    list(group = "region_annotation",      cols = region_colors,       title = "Region_Annotations"),
    list(group = "compartment_annotation", cols = compartment_colors,  title = "Compartment_Annotations"),
    list(group = "location_annotation",    cols = location_colors,     title = "Location_Annotations")
  )

  for (annot_info in spatial_annot_list) {
    for (img in available.images) {
      p <- SpatialDimPlot(merged.object,
                          group.by = annot_info$group,
                          images = img,
                          label = TRUE, repel = TRUE, label.size = 3,
                          pt.size.factor = 1.5,
                          cols = annot_info$cols) +
        ggtitle(paste("Spatial -", annot_info$title, "(16um) -", img)) +
        theme(legend.position = "right", legend.text = element_text(size = 7))

      fname <- paste0("output_16um/plots/spatial_", annot_info$title, "_", img, "_res2.pdf")
      ggsave(fname, plot = p, height = 10, width = 14)
      cat("Saved:", fname, "\n")
    }
  }

  cat("\nAnnotation plots saved to output_16um/plots/\n")

} else {
  cat("Warning: Annotation file not found:", annotation.file, "\n")
  cat("Expected CSV columns: Cluster, Annotation, Spatial.region.annotation,\n")
  cat("  Region.Annotation, Compartment, Color, Granular.annotation, Granular.color\n")
}
```

```{r epithelia_subset, fig.width=16, fig.height=12}
# UMAP colored by granular annotation
p_epi_gran <- DimPlot(epi.object,
```

## 9. RCTD Deconvolution with Annotated Master Single-Cell Reference

This section uses the annotated Master single-cell dataset (all cell types from
multiple reference datasets, annotated at resolution 1.2) to run a new round of
RCTD deconvolution on the 16um Visium HD data.

### 9.1 Load Master Reference and Prepare for RCTD

```{r master_rctd_load_ref}
# =============================================================================
# LOAD THE ANNOTATED MASTER SINGLE-CELL REFERENCE
# =============================================================================
library(spacexr)

master_path <- "output/master_integration/rds/Master.Obj.rds"
if (!file.exists(master_path)) {
  stop("Master object not found: ", master_path,
       "\nRun Master-dataset-integration.Rmd first.")
}

cat("Loading annotated Master single-cell reference...\n")
Master.Obj <- readRDS(master_path)
cat("Master object:", ncol(Master.Obj), "cells,", nrow(Master.Obj), "genes\n")

# Verify annotation column exists
if (!"cluster_annotation" %in% colnames(Master.Obj@meta.data)) {
  stop("cluster_annotation column not found in Master.Obj metadata.\n",
       "Run the annotation section in Master-dataset-integration.Rmd first.")
}

cat("\nCell type annotations (res 1.2):\n")
print(table(Master.Obj$cluster_annotation))
```

### 9.2 Build RCTD Reference

```{r master_rctd_build_ref}
# =============================================================================
# BUILD RCTD REFERENCE FROM MASTER OBJECT
# =============================================================================

cat("Building RCTD reference from Master object...\n")

# Use RNA assay raw counts
DefaultAssay(Master.Obj) <- "RNA"
Master.Obj <- JoinLayers(Master.Obj)

ref_counts <- GetAssayData(Master.Obj, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
ref_celltypes <- factor(Master.Obj$cluster_annotation)
names(ref_celltypes) <- colnames(Master.Obj)

# Remove cell types with too few cells and special labels
min_cells_per_type <- 25
remove_labels <- c("Unannotated", "Mix cluster remove", "Unidentified", "Unknown")

celltype_counts <- table(ref_celltypes)
valid_celltypes <- names(celltype_counts)[
  celltype_counts >= min_cells_per_type &
  !names(celltype_counts) %in% remove_labels
]

cat("Valid cell types (>=", min_cells_per_type, "cells, excluding special labels):",
    length(valid_celltypes), "\n")

removed <- setdiff(names(celltype_counts), valid_celltypes)
if (length(removed) > 0) {
  cat("Removed cell types:", paste(removed, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

# Filter
cells_to_keep <- names(ref_celltypes)[ref_celltypes %in% valid_celltypes]
ref_counts_filt <- ref_counts[, cells_to_keep]
ref_celltypes_filt <- droplevels(ref_celltypes[cells_to_keep])

# Ensure counts are integers (merged SCT objects may store non-integer RNA counts)
ref_counts_filt <- as(round(ref_counts_filt), "dgCMatrix")

# Sanitize cell type names — RCTD prohibits "/" in cell type labels
levels(ref_celltypes_filt) <- gsub("/", "-", levels(ref_celltypes_filt))

# Create RCTD Reference
master_reference_rctd <- Reference(
  counts = ref_counts_filt,
  cell_types = ref_celltypes_filt,
  nUMI = colSums(ref_counts_filt)
)

cat("RCTD Reference created:", ncol(ref_counts_filt), "cells,",
    length(levels(ref_celltypes_filt)), "cell types\n")

# Free Master.Obj
rm(Master.Obj, ref_counts, ref_counts_filt, ref_celltypes, ref_celltypes_filt)
gc()
```

### 9.3 Run RCTD Per Sample

```{r master_rctd_run}
# =============================================================================
# RUN RCTD ON EACH SAMPLE USING MASTER REFERENCE
# =============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fix for spacexr ".doSnowGlobals not found" error:
# doFuture (auto-loaded by future) deeply hijacks foreach's %dopar% dispatch.
# Clearing .foreachGlobals is not enough — doFuture re-registers itself.
# Nuclear fix: fully detach + unload the doFuture package so doSNOW can
# cleanly own %dopar%, then reload doFuture after RCTD completes.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
future::plan("sequential")

# Detach doFuture completely so it can't intercept %dopar%
if ("package:doFuture" %in% search()) {
  detach("package:doFuture", unload = TRUE, force = TRUE)
  cat("Detached doFuture package.\n")
}
if ("doFuture" %in% loadedNamespaces()) {
  try(unloadNamespace("doFuture"), silent = TRUE)
  cat("Unloaded doFuture namespace.\n")
}

# Clear any leftover foreach backend registration
env <- foreach:::.foreachGlobals
rm(list = ls(name = env), envir = env)

# Load doSNOW so spacexr's internal registerDoSNOW(cl) works cleanly
library(doSNOW)
library(foreach)

cat("Parallel backend reset for spacexr (doSNOW with 8 cores).\n")

merged.object <- JoinLayers(merged.object)

sample_images <- Images(merged.object)
cat("Running RCTD per sample with Master reference...\n")
cat("Samples:", paste(sample_images, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

master_rctd_results <- list()

for (img in sample_images) {
  cat("  Processing:", img, "\n")
  
  # Get spatial coords and counts for this image
  coords <- GetTissueCoordinates(merged.object, image = img)
  if ("cell" %in% colnames(coords)) {
    rownames(coords) <- coords$cell
  }
  spot_barcodes <- rownames(coords)
  counts <- GetAssayData(merged.object, assay = assay.name, layer = "counts")[, spot_barcodes, drop = FALSE]
  
  # Build coordinate data.frame
  numeric_cols <- colnames(coords)[sapply(coords, is.numeric)]
  coord_df <- data.frame(
    x = as.numeric(coords[[numeric_cols[1]]]),
    y = as.numeric(coords[[numeric_cols[2]]]),
    row.names = rownames(coords)
  )
  
  # Create SpatialRNA
  spatial_rctd <- SpatialRNA(
    coords = coord_df,
    counts = counts,
    nUMI = colSums(counts)
  )
  
  cat("    Spots:", ncol(counts), "\n")
  
  # Run RCTD (8 cores via spacexr's internal doSNOW parallelism)
  # tryCatch: if doSNOW still fails, fall back to single-core
  rctd <- tryCatch({
    r <- create.RCTD(spatial_rctd, master_reference_rctd, max_cores = 8)
    run.RCTD(r, doublet_mode = "full")
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("    WARNING: Parallel RCTD failed (", conditionMessage(e),
        "). Retrying with max_cores = 1...\n")
    r <- create.RCTD(spatial_rctd, master_reference_rctd, max_cores = 1)
    run.RCTD(r, doublet_mode = "full")
  })
  
  # Save per-sample result
  out_file <- paste0("output_16um/RDS-files/master_rctd_result_", img, ".RDS")
  saveRDS(rctd, file = out_file)
  cat("    Saved:", out_file, "\n")
  
  # Extract weights
  weights <- as.matrix(rctd@results[["weights"]])
  master_rctd_results[[img]] <- weights
  
  rm(rctd); gc()
}

cat("\nRCTD complete for all samples.\n")

# Restore parallel processing for downstream Seurat operations
future::plan("multicore", workers = 8)
cat("Restored future::plan('multicore') with 8 workers.\n")
```

### 9.4 Add Master RCTD Results to Seurat Object

```{r master_rctd_add_metadata}
# =============================================================================
# COMBINE MASTER RCTD RESULTS AND ADD TO SEURAT OBJECT
# =============================================================================

cat("Combining Master RCTD results...\n")

# If results not in memory, reload from disk
if (length(master_rctd_results) == 0) {
  sample_images <- Images(merged.object)
  for (img in sample_images) {
    rctd_file <- paste0("output_16um/RDS-files/master_rctd_result_", img, ".RDS")
    if (file.exists(rctd_file)) {
      rctd <- readRDS(rctd_file)
      master_rctd_results[[img]] <- as.matrix(rctd@results[["weights"]])
      rm(rctd)
    }
  }
  gc()
}

# Combine all weights
combined_weights <- do.call(rbind, master_rctd_results)
cat("Combined weights:", nrow(combined_weights), "spots x", ncol(combined_weights), "cell types\n")

# Normalize to sum to 1
weights_norm <- sweep(combined_weights, 1, rowSums(combined_weights), "/")
weights_norm[is.nan(weights_norm)] <- 0

# Add to metadata with M_RCTD_ prefix (to distinguish from original RCTD)
deconv_df <- as.data.frame(weights_norm)
colnames(deconv_df) <- paste0("M_RCTD_", gsub("[^[:alnum:]]", "_", colnames(deconv_df)))

common_cells <- intersect(rownames(deconv_df), colnames(merged.object))
cat("Matching cells:", length(common_cells), "of", nrow(deconv_df), "\n")

merged.object <- AddMetaData(merged.object, metadata = deconv_df[common_cells, , drop = FALSE])

# Dominant cell type
dominant_ct <- apply(weights_norm[common_cells, ], 1, function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x)) || sum(x) == 0) return("Unknown")
  colnames(weights_norm)[which.max(x)]
})

merged.object <- AddMetaData(merged.object,
                              metadata = data.frame(M_RCTD_dominant_celltype = dominant_ct,
                                                    row.names = names(dominant_ct)))
merged.object@meta.data$M_RCTD_dominant_celltype[
  is.na(merged.object@meta.data$M_RCTD_dominant_celltype)] <- "Unknown"

cat("\nMaster RCTD metadata added.\n")
cat("Unique dominant cell types:", length(unique(merged.object$M_RCTD_dominant_celltype)), "\n")

# Save updated object
saveRDS(merged.object, file = "output_16um/RDS-files/final_analysis_object_16um_with_master_deconv.RDS")
cat("Saved: final_analysis_object_16um_with_master_deconv.RDS\n")
```

### 9.5 Master Deconvolution — Visualization Setup

```{r master_deconv_setup}
# =============================================================================
# COLOR PALETTE AND COLUMN SETUP
# =============================================================================

m_rctd_cols <- grep("^M_RCTD_", colnames(merged.object@meta.data), value = TRUE)
m_rctd_cols <- m_rctd_cols[m_rctd_cols != "M_RCTD_dominant_celltype"]

cat("Master RCTD proportion columns:", length(m_rctd_cols), "\n")

# Build cell type color mapping
m_celltype_names <- gsub("M_RCTD_", "", m_rctd_cols)
m_dominant_cts <- unique(merged.object$M_RCTD_dominant_celltype)
m_dominant_cts <- m_dominant_cts[!is.na(m_dominant_cts)]
m_all_cts <- sort(unique(c(m_celltype_names, m_dominant_cts)))
m_all_cts <- m_all_cts[m_all_cts != "Unknown"]

# Generate enough colors for all cell types
# Use custom_colors first, then extend with hcl palette if needed
n_cts <- length(m_all_cts)
if (n_cts <= length(custom_colors)) {
  base_palette <- unname(custom_colors[seq_len(n_cts)])
} else {
  base_palette <- c(
    unname(custom_colors),
    grDevices::hcl.colors(n_cts - length(custom_colors), palette = "Dark 3")
  )
}

m_ct_colors <- setNames(base_palette, m_all_cts)
m_ct_colors["Unknown"] <- "#D3D3D3"

cat("Cell types:", n_cts, "\n")
cat("Colors assigned:", sum(!is.na(m_ct_colors)), "of", length(m_ct_colors), "\n")
```

### 9.10 Master Deconvolution — Bar Plots by Spatial Annotations

```{r master_deconv_barplots_annotations, fig.width=16, fig.height=12}
# =============================================================================
# BAR PLOTS GROUPED BY SPATIAL ANNOTATIONS (cluster / region / location / celltype)
# =============================================================================

annotation_cols <- c("cluster_annotation", "region_annotation",
                     "location_annotation", "celltype_annotation")
available_annots <- annotation_cols[annotation_cols %in% colnames(merged.object@meta.data)]

cat("Generating Master RCTD bar plots by annotations:", paste(available_annots, collapse = ", "), "\n")

for (annot_col in available_annots) {
  annot_values <- merged.object@meta.data[[annot_col]]
  if (all(is.na(annot_values))) next
  
  title_annot <- gsub("_", " ", tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_annotation", "", annot_col)))
  
  # Mean proportions
  mean_df <- merged.object@meta.data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[annot_col]])) %>%
    select(all_of(annot_col), all_of(m_rctd_cols)) %>%
    group_by(.data[[annot_col]]) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_longer(-all_of(annot_col), names_to = "celltype", values_to = "proportion")
  mean_df$celltype <- gsub("M_RCTD_", "", mean_df$celltype)
  
  p_mean <- ggplot(mean_df, aes(x = .data[[annot_col]], y = proportion, fill = celltype)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = m_ct_colors) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(title = paste("Master RCTD — Proportions by", title_annot, "(16um)"),
         x = title_annot, y = "Mean Proportion", fill = "Cell Type") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
  
  # Normalized bar plot
  p_norm <- ggplot(mean_df, aes(x = .data[[annot_col]], y = proportion, fill = celltype)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = m_ct_colors) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(title = paste("Master RCTD — Composition by", title_annot, "(%, 16um)"),
         x = title_annot, y = "Percentage", fill = "Cell Type") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
  
  # Dominant cell type
  dom_df <- merged.object@meta.data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[annot_col]]) & !is.na(M_RCTD_dominant_celltype)) %>%
    count(.data[[annot_col]], M_RCTD_dominant_celltype) %>%
    group_by(.data[[annot_col]]) %>%
    mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)
  
  p_dom <- ggplot(dom_df, aes(x = .data[[annot_col]], y = pct, fill = M_RCTD_dominant_celltype)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = m_ct_colors) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(title = paste("Master RCTD — Dominant Cell Type by", title_annot, "(16um)"),
         x = title_annot, y = "%", fill = "Dominant") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
  
  combined <- (p_mean | p_norm) / p_dom +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1)) +
    plot_annotation(title = paste("Master RCTD Deconvolution by", title_annot, "(16um)"))
  
  ggsave(paste0("output_16um/plots/master_deconv_barplot_by_", annot_col, ".pdf"),
         plot = combined, height = 14, width = 18)
  
  # Save tables
  mean_wide <- mean_df %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = celltype, values_from = proportion)
  write.csv(mean_wide,
            paste0("output_16um/tables/master_deconv_proportions_by_", annot_col, ".csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  
  cat("  Saved:", annot_col, "\n")
}
```

### 9.11 Master Deconvolution — Dominant Cell Type Summary

```{r master_deconv_dominant_summary, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# =============================================================================
# SUMMARY: DOMINANT CELL TYPE DISTRIBUTION
# =============================================================================

cat("Generating Master RCTD dominant cell type summary...\n")

# Overall summary
dom_summary <- merged.object@meta.data %>%
  count(M_RCTD_dominant_celltype) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

print(dom_summary)
write.csv(dom_summary, "output_16um/tables/master_deconv_dominant_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Dominant by sample
dom_by_sample <- merged.object@meta.data %>%
  count(orig.ident, M_RCTD_dominant_celltype) %>%
  group_by(orig.ident) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)

p_dom_sample <- ggplot(dom_by_sample,
                       aes(x = orig.ident, y = pct, fill = M_RCTD_dominant_celltype)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = m_ct_colors) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Master RCTD — Dominant Cell Type Distribution by Sample (16um)",
       x = "Sample", y = "%", fill = "Dominant Cell Type") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7))

ggsave("output_16um/plots/master_deconv_dominant_by_sample.pdf",
       plot = p_dom_sample, height = 10, width = 14)

# Save final object
saveRDS(merged.object, file = "output_16um/RDS-files/final_analysis_object_16um_with_master_deconv.RDS")

cat("\n=== MASTER RCTD DECONVOLUTION COMPLETE (16um) ===\n")
cat("Outputs in output_16um/plots/master_deconv_*.pdf\n")
cat("Tables in output_16um/tables/master_deconv_*.csv\n")
```

## Analysis Notes and Next Steps

### Key Differences from 8um Analysis:
1. **Larger bin size**: 16um bins contain ~4x the area of 8um bins
2. **Higher UMI counts**: Expect higher counts per spot due to larger bins
3. **Lower spatial resolution**: Trade-off between sensitivity and resolution
4. **Fewer total spots**: Fewer but more informative spots per sample

### Key Outputs:
1. **RDS files**: Saved Seurat objects in `output_16um/RDS-files/`
2. **Plots**: Visualization files in `output_16um/plots/`
3. **Tables**: Marker genes and compositions in `output_16um/tables/`
4. **Summary**: JSON file with analysis parameters

### Master RCTD Deconvolution Output Files (Section 9):
- `master_deconv_dominant_<sample>.pdf` - Dominant cell type per sample (spatial)
- `master_deconv_proportion_<celltype>_<sample>.pdf` - Per-cell-type proportion spatial plots
- `master_deconv_heatmap_cluster_res2.pdf` - Heatmap by cluster
- `master_deconv_heatmap_sample.pdf` - Heatmap by sample
- `master_deconv_barplot_by_sample.pdf` / `_by_cluster.pdf` - Bar plots
- `master_deconv_barplot_by_<annotation>.pdf` - Bar plots by spatial annotations
- `master_deconv_dominant_summary.csv` - Summary table
- `master_deconv_dominant_by_sample.pdf` - Dominant cell type by sample

### Recommended Next Steps:
1. **Compare with 8um analysis**: Identify resolution-dependent patterns
2. **Biological Interpretation**: Annotate clusters based on marker genes
3. **Functional Analysis**: Perform pathway enrichment on cluster markers
4. **Spatial Analysis**: Investigate spatial relationships between clusters
5. **Integration**: Combine insights from different bin sizes

### Customization Options:
- Adjust QC thresholds based on 16um bin characteristics
- Modify clustering resolutions for optimal granularity
- Compare clustering results with 8um analysis
- Include additional spatial analysis methods

This workflow provides analysis at 16um resolution, which is useful for:
- Reducing computational load
- Getting a broader overview of spatial patterns
- Identifying major tissue domains
- Preliminary exploration before detailed 8um or 2um analysis
